title.en: Analog meters: PMMC movement, ammeter and voltmeter
title.kn: ಅನಲಾಗ್ ಮೀಟರ್‌ಗಳು: PMMC ಚಲನೆ, ಅಮ್ಮೀಟರ್ ಮತ್ತು ವೋಲ್ಟ್‌ಮೀಟರ್

hook.en: The sensitive coil inside an analog meter burns out at about a milliampere. Yet the same meter can read 10 amperes or 500 volts. The secret is a well-chosen resistor.
hook.kn: ಅನಲಾಗ್ ಮೀಟರ್ ಒಳಗಿನ ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮ ಸುರುಳಿ ಸುಮಾರು ಒಂದು ಮಿಲಿಆಂಪಿಯರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಸುಟ್ಟುಹೋಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಆದರೂ ಅದೇ ಮೀಟರ್ 10 ಆಂಪಿಯರ್ ಅಥವಾ 500 ವೋಲ್ಟ್ ಓದಬಲ್ಲದು. ರಹಸ್ಯ: ಸರಿಯಾಗಿ ಆರಿಸಿದ ರೋಧಕ.

narration.en: The sensitive coil inside an analog meter burns out at about a milliampere. Yet the same meter can read 10 amperes or 500 volts. The secret is a well-chosen resistor.
narration.kn: ಅನಲಾಗ್ ಮೀಟರ್ ಒಳಗಿನ ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮ ಸುರುಳಿ ಸುಮಾರು ಒಂದು ಮಿಲಿಆಂಪಿಯರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಸುಟ್ಟುಹೋಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಆದರೂ ಅದೇ ಮೀಟರ್ 10 ಆಂಪಿಯರ್ ಅಥವಾ 500 ವೋಲ್ಟ್ ಓದಬಲ್ಲದು. ರಹಸ್ಯ: ಸರಿಯಾಗಿ ಆರಿಸಿದ ರೋಧಕ.

body.en: In a permanent magnet moving coil (PMMC) instrument, a light rectangular coil wound on an aluminium former is pivoted between the poles of a permanent magnet, around a soft-iron core. Current in the coil produces a deflecting torque proportional to the current. Two hairsprings give a controlling torque proportional to the deflection, and eddy currents in the aluminium former give damping. So the deflection θ ∝ I: the scale is linear. PMMC meters respond to d.c. only.

points.en: Linear scale, d.c. only, very sensitive

narration.en: In a PMMC meter, the current in a coil between magnet poles makes a torque, springs balance it, and the pointer deflection is proportional to the current. It reads d.c. only.
narration.kn: PMMC ಮೀಟರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಕಾಂತ ಧ್ರುವಗಳ ನಡುವಿನ ಸುರುಳಿಯ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಟಾರ್ಕ್ ಉಂಟುಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ; ಸ್ಪ್ರಿಂಗ್‌ಗಳು ಅದನ್ನು ಸಮತೋಲನಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಸೂಚಿಯ ವಿಚಲನ ಪ್ರವಾಹಕ್ಕೆ ಅನುಪಾತೀಯ. ಇದು ನೇರ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಮಾತ್ರ ಓದುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: From galvanometer to ammeter and voltmeter

say.en: A PMMC meter: a light coil sits between the poles of a permanent magnet. The current makes a torque, the springs oppose it, and the pointer settles at a deflection proportional to the current.
To make an ammeter, put a small shunt resistance in parallel. Most of the current bypasses the coil.
The shunt takes I minus I g, and the coil takes I g. Equal voltages across both give the shunt formula.
To make a voltmeter, put a large resistance in series. Then the full-scale current flows at the full-scale voltage.

title.en: Ammeter and voltmeter from a galvanometer

body.en: A galvanometer of resistance G gives full-scale deflection for a current I_g. To read up to a current I, connect a low resistance (shunt) in parallel: $R_{sh} = I_g G/(I - I_g)$. The ammeter is connected in series and has a very low resistance. To read up to a voltage V, connect a high resistance in series: $R_s = V/I_g - G$. The voltmeter is connected in parallel and has a high resistance. The sensitivity of a voltmeter is $1/I_g$ ohms per volt: a 50 µA movement gives 20 kΩ/V.

points.en: Ammeter: shunt in parallel, meter in series with circuit
Voltmeter: high R in series, meter across the load

narration.en: A shunt in parallel turns the galvanometer into an ammeter; a large series resistance turns it into a voltmeter. Voltmeter sensitivity is one over I g, in ohms per volt.
narration.kn: ಸಮಾಂತರ ಶಂಟ್ ಗ್ಯಾಲ್ವನೋಮೀಟರ್ ಅನ್ನು ಅಮ್ಮೀಟರ್ ಆಗಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ದೊಡ್ಡ ಸರಣಿ ರೋಧ ಅದನ್ನು ವೋಲ್ಟ್‌ಮೀಟರ್ ಆಗಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ವೋಲ್ಟ್‌ಮೀಟರ್ ಸಂವೇದನೆ = 1/I_g ಓಮ್ ಪ್ರತಿ ವೋಲ್ಟ್.

problem.en: A galvanometer has G = 100 Ω and gives full-scale deflection at 1 mA. Convert it into (a) an ammeter of range 0–1 A and (b) a voltmeter of range 0–10 V.

steps.en: R_sh = 0.1/0.999 ≈ 0.100 Ω, connected in parallel with the galvanometer.
(b) R_s = V/I_g − G = 10/0.001 − 100 = 9900 Ω, connected in series.

answer.en: (a) 0.1 Ω shunt in parallel; (b) 9.9 kΩ in series

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A galvanometer has G = 100 Ω and gives full-scale deflection at 1 mA. Convert it into (a) an ammeter of range 0–1 A and (b) a voltmeter of range 0–10 V.

body.en: To make an Ammeter, add a small resistance in Parallel (shunt). To make a Voltmeter, add a big resistance in Series. Then use them the other way round: the ammeter goes in series with the circuit, the voltmeter in parallel with the part.

narration.en: A-P, V-S. To make an Ammeter, add a small resistance in Parallel (shunt). To make a Voltmeter, add a big resistance in Series. Then use them the other way round: the ammeter goes in series with the circuit, the voltmeter in parallel with the part.

mnemonic.en: Ammeter = Parallel shunt; Voltmeter = Series resistor
